safety_tips.tip: Always keep valuables in front zip bags or anti-theft backpacks.
Use official taxi apps or hotel-arranged transfers.
Keep passport copies separate from originals.
Be cautious in crowded tourist hotspots and transport hubs.
Stick to well-lit areas at night, especially near canals or stations.
Watch out for fake police calls claiming unpaid fines or immigration issues.
Beware of 'ticket inspector' scams on trams asking for instant cash payments.
Avoid fake charity petitions near tourist areas, especially Amsterdam Central.
Watch for pickpocket distraction teams in crowded areas such as train stations and canals.
Be cautious of fake SIM or taxi overcharging near Schiphol Airport.
Never walk in bicycle lanes — cyclists have priority and move fast.

connectivity_tips.tip: Recommended SIM options: Vodafone Netherlands Prepaid SIM (strong city and regional coverage), KPN Prepaid SIM (best overall network reliability), Lebara Netherlands SIM (budget-friendly data packs), Orange Holiday Europe SIM (multi-country coverage).
eSIM works seamlessly in the Netherlands and is recommended for convenience.
Free Wi-Fi is widely available in cafés, museums, and stations. Coverage is excellent even in small towns like Haarlem.
eSIM is the most convenient option for multi-country travel — no physical SIM swap needed.
Always carry a power bank for full-day sightseeing and navigation. Download offline maps before long train journeys or cruises.
Most cafés, hotels, and museums offer free Wi-Fi but speeds vary. Google Maps, DB Navigator, and STIB apps require constant data access.

health_tips._source_file: Netherlands/All Inclusive Guide- Netherlands and Belgium.pdf

health_tips.tip: No special travel vaccinations are mandatory for Indian travellers to the Netherlands, Belgium, or Germany. All three countries have excellent healthcare systems.
Ensure routine vaccinations are up to date: Tetanus, Diphtheria, Polio, MMR (Measles, Mumps, Rubella), and seasonal Influenza.
Recommended optional vaccinations for travel: Hepatitis A (exposure through food/travel dining), Hepatitis B (optional for long stays), Typhoid (broader travel hygiene protection).
Tap water is safe to drink in all destinations.
Carry basic medications for cold, fever, and stomach upset. Use hand sanitizer regularly, especially in public transport and markets.
Stay hydrated, especially during walking-heavy sightseeing days. Wear comfortable footwear to avoid strain from cobblestone streets.
Use sunscreen even in mild May weather — UV exposure is still present.
Mosquito risk is very low, but mild repellents can be useful in parks. If prone to allergies, carry antihistamines due to spring pollen exposure.

Suggested travel medical kit: Paracetamol/pain reliever, antacids/digestion tablets, motion sickness tablets (for trains and canal/Rhine cruises), band-aids and antiseptic cream, ORS (oral rehydration salts), and personal prescription medicines with copy of prescription.

Excellent hospitals and pharmacies are widely available in all cities. Pharmacies are marked as 'Apotheek' in Netherlands/Belgium and 'Apotheke' in Germany. English-speaking staff are common in major cities.
